To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have formulated a problem of joint optimization of subset of SUs to be chosen for spectrum sensing and the number of spectral measurements to be collected by each of the chosen SUs.

the SPRT at the FC, in conjunction with the DSO based algorithms for the selection of the subset of SAs and the number of measurements to collect by each SU, is an effective approach for spectrum sensing in cognitive radios.

we propose an optimization framework for selection of SU subset and the number of spectral samples each of them needs to collect, based on the sequential probability ratio test, and demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed approach as against a fixed sample size approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of joint design of the set of SUs and their number of samples for spectrum sensing.

the problem of joint selection of subset of SUs, and the number of measurements they need to collect, to enable accurate spectrum sensing at the FC based on the energy measurement reports received from the SUs.

the problem of joint selection of subset of secondary users and the number of measurements each of the selected SU needs to collect, to maximize the composite cost function, subject to a constraint on the average number of measurements per SU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach based on SPPT provides a better performance as compared to the existing approaches in literature.

the SPRT based optimization of SU subset and the number of measurements they need to collect, is much more efficient in terms of the number of samples required, as against the fixed sample size test based optimization of the same parameters, for the same values of detection and false alarm probabilities.
the proposed optimization algorithm is able to provide significant gains in the average number of required samples as well as in the tracking ability of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed an optimization framework for selection of SAs and the number of measurements they need to collect for spectrum sensing in cognitive wireless networks, based on SPRT.
the proposed optimization based approach for spectrum sensing in a cognitive radio network is able to achieve a much lower number of samples for detection than that of the fixed size sample approach.

, by using an SPRT based spectrum sensing at the FC we can reduce the number of samples required from the SUs, and by using the proposed DSO approach we can achieve a better tracking ability of the SUs in response to variations of channel gains between the FC and the SUs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed optimization approach can be used to design efficient spectrum sensing protocols for cognitive radio networks.
the proposed DSO algorithms can be used for optimal selection of SUs, and for the number of samples to be collected by the SUs for spectrum sensing in CRNs.
, for a given set of SUs and a given number of samples collected at each of them, the performance of the FC is limited by the worst channel gain between the SUs to the FC.
